sections.overview: The Sarmatian yellow underwing is a noctuid moth recorded across Europe and parts of western Asia.
sections.identification: It is easily confused with the related Noctua orbona; a diffuse brown subapical mark helps separate it, but genital examination may be decisive.
sections.habitat: French records include mountain localities in the Pyrenees, Alps and Massif Central, while the species has been reported farther north and east.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on various low-growing herbaceous plants.
sections.behavior: Adults are recorded from June to October in central European accounts.
sections.reproduction: The caterpillar occurs from autumn into spring and overwinters, according to the German species account.
sections.ecology: Compared with Noctua comes, it has a broader black band on the hindwing and a larger central spot.
sections.conservation: French observations suggest recent expansion into new regions, but the sources reviewed do not provide a global population assessment.
